extracted.intended_audience: conference program committee members, conference organizers, researchers and newcomers interested in the consistency and statistics of peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Analyze consistency of conference peer review decisions using a duplicated-papers experiment and statistical models (binomial/multinomial, Bayesian) to estimate inconsistency, accept/reject precision, agreed accept rate, and their uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistency (proportion of differing decisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proportion of decisions that were not the same across the two independent committees (computed from the confusion matrix). Example: 43 out of 166 papers -> 0.259 (25.9%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreted as the probability that a submitted paper would receive a different decision under an independent re-run of the process. Compute from duplicated-paper confusion matrix; report as proportion and include uncertainty from statistical modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Probability that a paper accepted by one committee would be accepted by the other (e.g. Committee 1 estimate 22/(22+22)=0.50, Committee 2 21/(22+21)=0.49; averaged ~49.5%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute per committee and/or average across committees. Use Monte Carlo/Bayesian sampling to provide error bars (example: 0.51 ± 0.13 reported).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Probability that a paper rejected by one committee would also be rejected by the other (e.g. Committee 1 101/(22+101)=0.82, Committee 2 101/(21+101)=0.83; average ~82.5%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute analogously to accept precision; present uncertainties (example: 0.82 ± 0.05 from sampling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed accept rate
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure such as the ratio of consistent accepts to consistent rejects or the proportion of papers that were consistently accepted across committees (example: 22/123 = 0.18 or reported as 0.18 ± 0.07).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be computed from counts of consistent accept / (consistent accept + consistent reject) or other agreed-accept definitions; estimate uncertainty via posterior sampling and report histograms or error bars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multinomial outcome probabilities (consistent accept / inconsistent / consistent reject)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model the three possible outcomes for each duplicated paper (consistent accept, inconsistent decision, consistent reject) with a multinomial and estimate the probabilities under a Bayesian Dirichlet prior. Example posterior means: consistent accept 0.136 ± 0.06, inconsistent 0.260 ± 0.09, consistent reject 0.60 ± 0.15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Dirichlet prior (e.g. α_i = 1 uninformative) as conjugate to the multinomial; compute posterior Dirichlet parameters α + k and derive posterior mean and variance using provided formulas. Report credible intervals and discuss prior choice sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominator choice for accept probability calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use as a denominator the number of papers that were initially sent for review (not just those with final PC decisions). For duplicated-paper stats the author used 170 as denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about denominator selection when reporting accept rates; differences (preliminary withdrawals, withdrawn before PC decision) materially affect computed rates and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random committee baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare observed statistics to a 'random conference' baseline where papers are accepted at random at the overall accept rate (e.g. at 25% expect inconsistency 37.5%, accept precision 25%, reject precision 75%, agreed accept rate 10%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute expected confusion matrix and derived metrics under random acceptance to contextualize observed performance. Use this baseline to judge whether committee behavior is better than chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design: duplicated papers and independent committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Select ~10% of submissions to be independently re-reviewed by a second, independent committee; randomly assign reviewers to committees, with program chairs ensuring expert coverage on both sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure random assignment of reviewers to committees to support inference about consistency; explicitly document any deviations (e.g., manual selection to ensure expertise) and how they might bias results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for administrative/awareness bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge and account for potential bias introduced when Area Chairs or administrators know which papers are duplicates (Area Chairs knew duplicates in this experiment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State procedures to limit preferential treatment; examine whether knowledge of duplicates could affect outcomes and, if necessary, model or test for such bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical modeling choices and uncertainty quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate probability models (binomial for single accept-rate questions, multinomial for three outcome counts) and Bayesian methods (Dirichlet prior conjugate to multinomial) to capture uncertainty; use Monte Carlo to estimate derived ratio distributions (accept/reject precision, agreed accept rate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document model assumptions, choice of priors (uninformative vs informative), and whether analysis is sensitivity analysis or a full process model. Provide histograms, error bars, and discuss whether random-baseline values fall inside credible ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior selection and sensitivity analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the effect of prior beliefs on posterior estimates (e.g., uninformative Dirichlet vs priors reflecting knowledge that inconsistency is unlikely to exceed random-committee worst case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform sensitivity checks with different priors or model structures, and be explicit when analysis is intended only to quantify sampling uncertainty rather than to model decision-generating mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Type I and Type II errors given accept rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame reviewer disagreements in terms of Type I (accept a paper that should be rejected) and Type II (reject a paper that should be accepted) errors; observe that with low accept rates Type I errors become more common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting inconsistency, consider how conference selectivity changes relative frequencies of error types; document whether committee deliberations prioritize controlling Type I or Type II errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of additional data (paper scores) for richer modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary-count analysis ignores richer information such as individual paper scores and reviewer comments; including scores enables more detailed models to explain inconsistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If available, incorporate review scores, reviewer confidence, and other metadata into models to better estimate sources of disagreement and to separate sampling noise from systematic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational timeline and process for running review
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and publish a structured timeline for area chair recruitment, reviewer recruitment, bidding, reviewing, author rebuttal, teleconferences, and final decisions (dates/waves were listed for NIPS 2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document recruitment waves, bidding windows, review start/end, rebuttal period, teleconference windows, and decision dates so that experimental treatments and temporal effects can be interpreted; deviations (e.g., recruiting reviewers after deadline) should be noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for sample size limitations and communicate uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that a limited number of duplicated papers produces substantial uncertainty in derived metrics; e.g. wide credible intervals around accept/reject precisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report error bars or credible intervals, avoid overinterpreting point estimates, and consider increasing duplicated-sample size in future experiments to narrow uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Monte Carlo and visualization to assess derived-statistic distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: For complex derived statistics (ratios of multinomial probabilities), use Monte Carlo sampling from the posterior to estimate means, variances, medians, and histograms; compare empirical densities to random-baseline lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce histograms and indicate baseline expectations on plots; report summary statistics (mean ± 2√var, medians, percentiles) and verify shape/symmetry of distributions before choosing summary metrics.
